name: InfinityDB
tagline: Boiler Bay's all-Java embedded B-tree database with a ConcurrentNavigableMap API and a server edition.
description: InfinityDB is a commercial all-Java database engine from Boiler Bay Software. Its core is the ItemSpace, a sorted set of variable-length items made of typed components stored in a single file through a lockless concurrent B-tree; on top of that it exposes an extended java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentNavigableMap, so nested, multi-valued maps can model tables, documents, graphs or text indexes in one database. It offers global durable commits or fine-grained optimistic ACID transactions, and the Encrypted edition adds AES-256 with HMAC-SHA256. InfinityDB Server adds shared remote access with REST, web administration and PatternQuery, and is sold on AWS Marketplace or for on-premises use. Licensing is commercial, with free time-limited trials.

pricing.notes: Embedded and Encrypted editions licensed directly from Boiler Bay; Server via AWS Marketplace or on-prem; free time-limited trials.

scale.notes: Single-file embedded store with no fixed size limit; the server edition shares it over the network.

strengths: Standard ConcurrentNavigableMap interface over a persistent, concurrent B-tree
One file can hold relational, document, graph and text-index structures
Optimistic fine-grained ACID transactions with automatic conflict detection
Encrypted edition with AES-256 and HMAC-SHA256
weaknesses: Commercial license with no published pricing
Small vendor and community; little public news since the late 2010s
useCases: Embedded storage in Java applications and appliances
Text indexing and custom data structures inside one file
Industrial data collection on JVM devices
